Android does not guarantee a gap-free block to any normal app. Some manufacturers stop background services, and you can turn the service off at any time. The reminder is meant to help you, not to watch you.
To turn it off: Settings › Accessibility › Handyzeitvertreib.

Android logs when an app comes to the foreground and leaves it again. Handyzeitvertreib reads these entries and adds up the times. The log is not a live stream: values are as current as the last refresh.

Without the extra service the app checks roughly every 15 minutes and notifies you. With the optional accessibility service, the reminder screen appears when you open an app whose limit is reached. Normal Android apps cannot create a block that cannot be bypassed.
Android batches background work to save battery. In battery saver or Doze, the check may run later.
An extension is only granted after successful confirmation through Android. The app only learns whether confirmation succeeded, never your biometric data.
If both an app\'s own limit and a group limit apply, the one with less time left takes effect. In totals, each app is only counted once.
A day starts at midnight in your device\'s current time zone. On days with a clock change it is 23 or 25 hours long.
Some manufacturers stop background services very aggressively or name settings differently. If reminders do not arrive, check the battery settings for Handyzeitvertreib.
A calm message when a planned time is over.
